explanation.text:
Excepting the recurrence of the refrain, there is no good reason to suppose this a part of the preceding, though the scope is the same. It has always been placed separate. (Psa 43:1-5)

Judge--or, "vindicate" (Psa 10:18).

plead, etc.-- (Psa 35:1).

ungodly--neither in character or condition objects of God's favor (compare Psa 4:3).

bsb.text: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from deceitful and unjust men.

explanation.text:
God of my strength--by covenant relation my stronghold (Psa 18:1).

cast me off--in scorn.

because--or, "in," that is, in such circumstances of oppression.

bsb.text: For You are the God of my refuge. Why have You rejected me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?

explanation.text:
light--as in Psa 27:1.

truth--or, "faithfulness" (Psa 25:5), manifest it by fulfilling promises. Light and truth are personified as messengers who will bring him to the privileged place of worship.

tabernacles--plural, in allusion to the various courts.

bsb.text: Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to Your holy mountain and to the place where You dwell.

explanation.text:
the altar--as the chief place of worship. The mention of the harp suggests the prominence of praise in his offering.

Next: Psalms Chapter 44

bsb.text: Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.

explanation.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul?.... See Gill on Psalm 42:5 and See Gill on Psalm 42:11.

bsb.text: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
